# Voice report B — entries #25–#49 (Nangbi … King Muyeol)

Rewrites under "Short and memorable": sentences under ~12 words, at most two proper nouns per sentence and three per paragraph, same beat. `quote` blocks and the intentional exceptions are untouched. Block-0 author lines are left alone. Lines that read like Heewon's plain handwritten narration (flat textbook statements such as "Queen Jinduk is dead.") are marked **author line?**: they get a suggested rewrite but should only change with her sign-off.

Block numbers are top-level indices in the current `story.json`. Where `audit-names.json` was built on an older layout, the block is given as `b<flashback>.<inner>`.

---

### Nangbi (#25)
- **b1** — names: 4 (Jinpyeong, Silla, Nangbi Fortress, Yushin). Why it glazes: it opens on a reign-year date, then crams the army, the fortress and the hero into one long sentence.
  - Before: "Autumn, King Jinpyeong’s fifty-first year. Silla’s army is breaking against the walls of Nangbi Fortress, and the men who are supposed to be charging are sitting down in the trenches instead…"
  - After (EN): "Autumn. Silla’s army is breaking against a Goguryeo wall. The men who should be charging are sitting in the trenches. Yushin is thirty-four, a banner captain. His white horse doesn’t even have a name."
  - After (KO): "가을. 신라군이 고구려의 성벽 앞에서 부서지고 있다. 돌격해야 할 병사들이 참호에 주저앉아 있다. 유신은 서른넷, 깃발 하나를 맡은 대장이다. 그의 흰 말에는 아직 이름도 없다."
- **b22** — names: 6 (Yeon, Pyongyang, High Commander, Gesomun, Taejo, Summit). Why it glazes: the family, the city, the office, the son and the father all arrive in the first sentence.
  - Before: "The Yeon family lives in Pyongyang these years, in the big house below the palace hill, because the High Commander is Gesomun’s father, Yeon Taejo. He has held the chair for ten years…"
  - After (EN): "Gesomun’s family lives in the big house below the palace hill. His father, Yeon Taejo, has run the Summit for ten years. Long enough to outlive most of the men who voted for him. None of the ones who voted against. Most nights he comes home in a silence the servants have learned to walk around."
  - After (KO): "개소문의 집안은 왕궁 언덕 아래 큰 집에 산다. 아버지 연태조는 십 년째 회의의 윗자리를 지키고 있다. 그를 밀어준 사람들이 대부분 먼저 죽을 만큼 긴 세월이다. 반대한 사람들은 하나도 안 죽었다. 거의 매일 밤 그는 말없이 돌아오고, 하인들은 그 침묵을 비켜 다니는 법을 익혔다."
- **b34** — names: 6 (Euija, Eight Great Clans, Chunchu, Harmony Council, Gesomun, Pyongyang). Why it glazes: three heroes and three institutions in two sentences, and the reader has to sort out which belongs to whom.
  - Before: "Euija learns the Eight Great Clans at his father’s table, and Chunchu learns the Harmony Council from the way it walked his grandfather off the throne and kept his father waiting outside its doors…"
  - After (EN): "Each of them learns his country at home. Euija learns the great clans at his father’s table. Chunchu learns the council from the day it walked his grandfather off the throne. And Gesomun learns this city here, from an old man reading one report three times by lamplight. Nobody else in the city would read it once."
  - After (KO): "셋 다 나라를 집에서 배운다. 의자는 아버지의 밥상머리에서 큰 가문들을 배운다. 춘추는 회의가 할아버지를 왕좌에서 걸어 내려보낸 그날에서 회의를 배운다. 그리고 개소문은 여기서 이 도시를 배운다. 등불 아래 같은 보고서를 세 번 읽는 늙은이에게서. 이 도시의 누구도 한 번 읽지 않을 보고서를."
- **b36** — names: 6 (Surabol, Goguryeo, Sword of Silla, Eternal General, Pyongyang, Silla). Why it glazes: the last sentence runs 40 words and swaps "Gesomun" for a title the reader has to decode.
  - Before: "That is where the name comes from. Not from Surabol, which likes its titles stamped and filed, but from the people he beat: Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning…"
  - After (EN): "That’s where the name comes from. Not from his own capital, which likes its titles stamped and filed. From the people he beat. Goguryeo calls him the Sword of Silla first, and means it as a warning. On the border, mothers use it to get children indoors before dark. Thirteen years later, Gesomun will hear that sword is riding for the prince in his prison. He’ll remember a hall, a report read twice, and his father reading it a third time."
  - After (KO): "그 이름은 거기서 나왔다. 칭호에 도장 찍어 철해 두기 좋아하는 제 나라 도읍에서가 아니다. 그에게 진 사람들에게서다. 고구려가 먼저 그를 신라의 검이라 부른다. 경고의 뜻으로. 국경의 어머니들은 해 지기 전 아이들을 불러들일 때 그 이름을 쓴다. 십삼 년 뒤, 개소문은 그 검이 자기 감옥의 왕자를 구하러 온다는 소식을 듣는다. 그는 한 전각을, 두 번 읽힌 보고서를, 그리고 그것을 세 번째로 읽던 아버지를 떠올릴 것이다."

### Forty Fortresses (#26)
- **b5** — names: 6 (Sabi, Sword of the Divine Country, Surabol, Hundred-Victories Gyebek, Yellow Mountain, Greatest Blade of Samhan). Why it glazes: two cities, two titles and a battle the reader hasn't reached yet. "Until Yellow Mountain" also gives away where the two of them will finally meet.
  - Before: "In Sabi markets they spit when they say Sword of the Divine Country. In Surabol they toast it. In both cities someone always adds, quietly, that Hundred-Victories Gyebek has not yet been measured against him…"
  - After (EN): "In Baekje’s markets they spit when they say his title. At home they toast it. Both sides add, quietly, that Gyebek hasn’t met him yet. Until he does, “greatest blade” is a tavern argument with two right answers."
  - After (KO): "백제 장터에선 그의 칭호를 말할 때 침을 뱉는다. 고향에선 축배를 든다. 양쪽 다 누군가 조용히 덧붙인다. 계백과는 아직 붙어 보지 않았다고. 붙기 전까지 ‘최강의 칼’은 정답이 둘인 주점 논쟁이다."

### The Eastern Star (#27)
- **b15** — names: 3 (Yeon, Jumong Cavern, 국동대혈) plus a hanja gloss in the English. Why it glazes: there is a gloss in the English line, and "where the holy king prayed when the river had no bridge" explains the Jumong myth before its own episode, which opens the box early.
  - Before: "Three nights after the banquet hall is scrubbed, Yeon climbs to Jumong Cavern — 국동대혈, where the holy king prayed when the river had no bridge. The marches believe the stone remembers bowstrings."
  - After (EN): "The banquet hall has been scrubbed for three nights. Yeon climbs to a cave in the hill above the river. Nobody prays there lightly. The marches say the stone still remembers bowstrings."
  - After (KO): "연회장의 피를 씻어 낸 지 사흘 밤. 연은 강 위 언덕의 동굴로 오른다. 그곳에선 아무도 가볍게 빌지 않는다. 변방 사람들은 그 돌이 아직 활시위 소리를 기억한다고 믿는다."

### Emperor (#28)
- **b0** — names: 3 (Epilogue · Part I, Chang’an, Second Emperor). Why it glazes: "Epilogue · Part I… the first syllable of Part II" is a structural signpost, and it reads as an editor's note, not the narrator. Skip this if it is one of Heewon's lines.
  - Before: "Epilogue · Part I. Chang’an. The Second Emperor turns a name over on his tongue — the first syllable of Part II."
  - After (EN): "Far to the west, a man who owns half the world hears a new name. He turns it over on his tongue, like a grape he hasn’t decided to eat."
  - After (KO): "저 멀리 서쪽, 천하의 절반을 가진 사내가 새 이름 하나를 듣는다. 그는 삼킬지 말지 아직 정하지 않은 포도알처럼 그 이름을 혀 위에서 굴린다."
- **b3** — this is the current teaser line. The card in `teasers-b.json` keeps it, polishes it and sets `replaceBlock: 3`.

### Four Dragons (#29)
- **b28** — names: 9 distinct (Han, Red Dragon, Ashina She’er, Turkic, White Dragon, Qibi Heli, Tiele, Heavenly Qaghan, Black Dragon, Zhangsun Wuji). Why it glazes: three foreign personal names, a tribe and a title in four sentences, and none of them comes back. The dragon colours already do the work.
  - Before: "Two of the four dragons are not Han at all. The Red Dragon is Ashina She’er, a prince of the Turkic royal clan who keeps his felt tents inside the capital walls; the White Dragon is Qibi Heli…"
  - After (EN): "Two of the four dragons were born on the steppe. The Red Dragon is a steppe prince who keeps felt tents inside the capital walls. The White Dragon walked his whole tribe across the border as a boy. The steppe has its own title for the emperor, and he answers to it. Even his favourite horses came from out there. The Black Dragon is the empress’s brother. He argued against this war in council. He’s riding to it anyway."
  - After (KO): "네 마리 용 가운데 둘은 초원에서 태어났다. 붉은 용은 도성 담장 안에 펠트 천막을 치고 사는 초원의 왕자다. 흰 용은 어린 나이에 부족 전체를 이끌고 국경을 넘어왔다. 초원은 황제를 따로 부르는 칭호가 있고, 그는 그 이름에 대답한다. 아끼는 말들마저 그쪽에서 왔다. 검은 용은 황후의 오라비다. 그는 회의에서 이 전쟁을 반대했다. 그리고 지금 그 전쟁으로 말을 달린다."
- **b24** — names: 4 (Seventh Invasion, Goguryeo, West, Laizhou) plus a muster catalogue. Why it glazes: the sentence boasts that the list is boring, then reads the list out anyway. (The first clause may be an author line; it is kept.)
  - Before: "He launches the Seventh Invasion of Goguryeo — the seventh time an army has come out of the West for it, and the first that he will lead himself. The muster is a catalogue the clerks take three days to read aloud…"
  - After (EN): "He launches the Seventh Invasion of Goguryeo. It’s the seventh army out of the West, and the first he leads himself. The clerks need three days to read the muster aloud. Horse from the frontier. Foot from the rivers. Five hundred hulls riding low with a year of grain."
  - After (KO): "그는 고구려 일곱 번째 침공을 일으킨다. 서쪽에서 온 일곱 번째 군대이고, 그가 직접 이끄는 첫 군대다. 서기들이 소집 명부를 소리 내어 읽는 데만 사흘이 걸린다. 변방의 기병. 강가 고을의 보병. 한 해 치 곡식을 싣고 낮게 뜬 배 오백 척."
- **b44** — names: 4 (Longmen, 絳州龍門, Xue Li, Rengui) plus a hanja gloss in English. Why it glazes: a gloss and a courtesy-name lesson stand between the reader and the farmer.
  - Before: "In a poor field of Longmen — 絳州龍門, millet and rammed earth, a hut that does not pretend to be a kiln — a farmer named Xue Li, courtesy name Rengui, is planning to rebury his ancestors…"
  - After (EN): "In a poor field at Longmen, a farmer named Xue Rengui is planning to rebury his ancestors. Millet, rammed earth, a hut that doesn’t pretend to be anything. He has the right soil for graves. He doesn’t yet know he has the wrong year for quiet."
  - After (KO): "용문의 척박한 밭에서 설인귀라는 농부가 조상의 무덤을 다시 쓰려 한다. 조밭, 다진 흙, 아무것도 아닌 척하지 않는 오두막. 무덤 쓸 흙은 제대로 골랐다. 조용히 살 해를 잘못 골랐다는 건 아직 모른다."
- **b59** — names: 3 (Liu, Liu Yingchun, Zhengshi). Why it glazes: the chronicler stops the scene to sort sources.
  - Before: "Stages a few centuries later will not leave Liu in the hut. They will put her in a cold kiln and give her a name the official histories never wrote — Liu Yingchun — and a line that is opera, not Zhengshi…"
  - After (EN): "Later opera won’t leave Liu in the hut. It puts her in a cold kiln and gives her a fuller name the histories never wrote. And a song. Lovely song. Not history."
  - After (KO): "훗날의 경극은 유씨를 오두막에 두지 않는다. 차가운 가마 속에 앉히고, 사서가 적지 않은 긴 이름을 붙여 준다. 노래도 하나. 좋은 노래다. 역사는 아니다."

### Yodong (#30)
- **b0** — names: 4 (Liao, Blue Dragon, Hyeondo ×2, Goguryeo). Why it glazes: the date, the river, the ford and a fort name the reader will never see again, all in one stretch.
  - Before: "Goguryeo has spent fourteen years building a wall of fortresses along the Liao, and the Blue Dragon goes around it. He shows his banners on the middle road, turns north in the night, and on the first day of the fourth month…"
  - After (EN): "Goguryeo has spent fourteen years building a wall of forts along the river. The Blue Dragon simply walks around it. He shows his banners on the middle road, then turns north in the night. By morning his horse are across an unwatched ford. The first fortress shuts its gates. It holds exactly as long as the gates do."
  - After (KO): "고구려는 십사 년 동안 강을 따라 성의 벽을 쌓았다. 청룡은 그 벽을 그냥 돌아간다. 가운데 길에 깃발을 보여 주고, 밤에 북으로 꺾는다. 아침이 되자 그의 기병은 아무도 지키지 않던 여울을 건너 있다. 첫 성이 문을 닫는다. 딱 그 문이 버티는 만큼만 버틴다."
- **b1** — names: 7 (Sinseong, New Fortress, Prince of Jiangxia, Blue Dragon, Gaemo, Yeon, Gasi). Why it glazes: three forts and a prince in four sentences.
  - Before: "Sinseong, the New Fortress, does not fall; the emperor’s cousin, the Prince of Jiangxia, spends ten days under its walls and comes away with nothing. So the Blue Dragon leaves a guard to watch it…"
  - After (EN): "The New Fortress doesn’t fall. The emperor’s cousin spends ten days under its walls and leaves with nothing. So the Blue Dragon posts a guard on it and turns south. The next fort lasts a little over ten days. Seven hundred men Yeon sent to hold it are taken in the gate. They ask to serve the emperor instead."
  - After (KO): "신성은 무너지지 않는다. 황제의 사촌이 열흘을 성 아래 머물다 빈손으로 물러난다. 그래서 청룡은 신성에 감시병을 남기고 남으로 돈다. 다음 성은 열흘 남짓 버틴다. 연이 지키라고 보낸 칠백 명이 성문에서 붙잡힌다. 그들은 대신 황제를 섬기겠다고 청한다."
- **b4** — names: 6 (Six Armies, Liao, Sui, Master of Works, Yan Lide, Second Emperor). Why it glazes: the engineer's name and office sit right in the middle of the best image in the paragraph.
  - Before: "Between the Six Armies and the walls lies the Liao marsh, two hundred li of mud where a Sui host once went in to the knee and came out as a song. The Master of Works, Yan Lide, lays earth across it…"
  - After (EN): "Between the army and the walls lies the Liao marsh. Two hundred li of mud. A Sui host once went in up to the knee and came out as a song. The emperor’s engineer lays a road of earth across it, wide enough for carts. When the last wagon is over, the emperor has the road torn up. Nobody goes home the way they came. He wants every man in the column to know it."
  - After (KO): "군대와 성벽 사이에 요하의 늪이 있다. 이백 리의 진흙. 수나라 대군이 무릎까지 빠져 들어갔다가 노래가 되어 나온 곳이다. 황제의 장인이 그 위에 수레가 다닐 만한 흙길을 깐다. 마지막 수레가 건너자 황제는 길을 걷어 내게 한다. 아무도 왔던 길로 돌아가지 못한다. 그는 대열의 모든 병사가 그걸 알기를 바란다."
- **b5** — names: 6 (Eastern Fortress, Yodong, Sui, Blue Dragon, Son of Heaven, Tang). Why it glazes: the 37-word moat sentence buries the best beat, the officers carrying two sacks.
  - Before: "Then the Eastern Fortress itself: Yodong, the city that held the Sui off for three summers and never opened. The Blue Dragon has already driven one sortie back through its gate when the emperor arrives…"
  - After (EN): "Then the Eastern Fortress itself. It held off the last dynasty for three summers and never opened. The Blue Dragon has already driven one sortie back through the gate when the emperor arrives. He rides to the moat with a sack of earth across his saddle and throws it in. His officers can’t be seen carrying less than him. They carry two. The army rings the walls a hundred deep and beats the drums until the ground answers."
  - After (KO): "그리고 동쪽의 성, 그 자체. 지난 왕조를 세 번의 여름 동안 막아 내고 끝내 열리지 않은 성이다. 황제가 도착했을 때 청룡은 이미 한 번의 출격을 성문 안으로 밀어 넣은 뒤다. 황제는 안장에 흙 자루 하나를 얹고 해자 끝까지 달려가 그것을 던져 넣는다. 장수들은 황제보다 적게 나르는 모습을 보일 수 없다. 그래서 두 자루씩 나른다. 군대는 성을 백 겹으로 둘러싸고 땅이 대답할 때까지 북을 친다."
- **b11** — names: 3 (Holy King, Blue Dragon, Tang). Why it glazes: the sack ends in a ledger of four numbers in a row.
  - Before: "The Holy King is not consulted again. The Blue Dragon’s stone-throwers put rocks the size of grain jars three hundred paces over the walls… they kill ten thousand men and take ten thousand soldiers, forty thousand townspeople and five hundred thousand sacks of grain…"
  - After (EN): "The Holy King isn’t consulted again. The Blue Dragon’s throwers hurl rocks the size of grain jars over the walls. Towers roll up to the parapet. On the twelfth day a south wind rises. They fire the south-west tower, and the wind carries it into town. When the gate gives, the clerks count ten thousand dead, then lose interest and count the grain. The fortress a million men couldn’t open has lasted twelve days."
  - After (KO): "성왕께 다시 묻는 사람은 없다. 청룡의 포차가 독만 한 돌을 성벽 너머로 날린다. 공성탑이 성가퀴에 붙는다. 열이틀째 남풍이 인다. 그들이 서남쪽 망루에 불을 지르자 바람이 불길을 성안으로 실어 간다. 성문이 무너지자 서기들은 죽은 자를 만까지 세다가, 흥미를 잃고 곡식을 센다. 백만 대군이 열지 못한 성이 열이틀을 버텼다."
- **b18** — names: 11 (Tang, Baegam ×2, Yeon ×2, Ogol, White Dragon, Son Daeeum, Bisa, Sinseong, Geonan, Goguryeo). Why it glazes: a roll-call of forts the reader can't picture. The point is "the line falls", and the names hide it.
  - Before: "Meanwhile the rest of the line comes down like roof tiles, and the Tang clerks file it in a single column. At Baegam Yeon sends the Ogol garrison out to break the siege, and they put a spear into the White Dragon’s waist…"
  - After (EN): "Meanwhile the rest of the line comes down like roof tiles. The clerks file it in a single column. At one fort Yeon’s riders break out and put a spear into the White Dragon’s waist. He has it bound and is back in the saddle by evening. The fort’s lord opens the gate anyway. Out on the southern cape, the fleet takes another in a month. Of all the forts Yeon spent fourteen years hauling stone for, two still fly Goguryeo’s banners."
  - After (KO): "그 사이 나머지 성들은 기왓장처럼 떨어진다. 서기들은 그것을 한 줄로 철해 둔다. 한 성에서는 연의 기병이 뛰쳐나가 흰 용의 허리에 창을 꽂는다. 흰 용은 상처를 동여매고 저녁이면 다시 안장에 올라 있다. 성주는 어쨌든 문을 연다. 남쪽 곶에서는 수군이 한 달 만에 성 하나를 더 빼앗는다. 연이 십사 년 동안 돌을 날라 쌓은 성들 가운데 아직 고구려 깃발을 단 곳은 둘뿐이다."

### Boiling River (#31)
- **b0** — **author line?** names: 3 (Dongchun, Yodong, Biryu) plus a regnal number "(#11)" and a hanja gloss "沸流". Why it glazes: the house rule bans regnal numbers and glosses.
  - Before: "King Dongchun (#11) strikes the Yodong peninsula after a diplomatic spat. The war that comes back at him starts on the Biryu, a river whose name, 沸流, means boiling."
  - After (EN): "King Dongchun picks a fight over a diplomatic spat. The war that comes back at him starts on a river named for boiling."
  - After (KO): "동천왕은 외교 시비 하나로 싸움을 건다. 되돌아온 전쟁은 ‘끓는 강’이라는 이름의 강에서 시작된다."

### Stallion Mountain (#32)
- **b4** — names: 7 (Tang, Chinese, Sul Gedu, Silla, Goguryeo ×2, Left Militant Guard). Why it glazes: the unit name and the backstory are one 45-word sentence.
  - Before: "In the Tang line, among the guard captains, is a man whose Chinese still has the sea in it. Sul Gedu left Silla twenty-four winters ago in the hold of a merchant ship, and when the emperor called for men…"
  - After (EN): "In the Tang line stands a guard captain whose accent still has the sea in it. Sul Gedu left Silla twenty-four winters ago, in the hold of a merchant ship. When the emperor called for volunteers, he put his own name down. It’s the only way a foreigner gets a captain’s sash. Across the field, the enemy’s banners are close enough to read."

  - After (KO): "서현은 가야 사람이 도읍에서 오르는 방식으로 오른다. 한 계단씩, 매번 그 상자를 기억하는 누군가의 서명을 받으며. 마지막엔 나라의 셋째 품계에 이른다. 그는 대야성에 앉아 적과 마주한 변경을 다스린다. 아들의 비석은 그에게 다른 이름을 붙일 것이다. 사관은 둘 중 하나를 고르지 못하고, 둘 다 적고 넘어간다."

### 결 (結) (#44)
- **b17** — names: 6 (Yushin, Hwarang, Surabol Son, Musan, Gurema, Bidam). Why it glazes: three lineage names in narration, and the dialogue at b18 says them again anyway.
  - Before: "Yushin does not kneel. Mud still wet, he turns to the Hwarang who followed him out and names a house — Surabol Son, Musan, the Gurema line Bidam carried in his jaw and never once claimed aloud."
  - After (EN): "Yushin does not kneel. Mud still wet, he turns to the Hwarang behind him and names a house. Bidam’s own line. The one he carried in his jaw and never once claimed aloud."
  - After (KO): "유신은 무릎 꿇지 않는다. 진흙이 마르기도 전에 그는 뒤따른 화랑들을 돌아보고 한 집안의 이름을 댄다. 비담의 핏줄. 비담이 턱 안에 물고 다니면서도 한 번도 입 밖에 내지 않은 그 핏줄."
- **b1** — "which a Sangdaedeung does not do". Use the English title the rest of the book uses: "which a High Councillor does not do". KO stays 상대등.

### Queen Jinduk (#45)
- **b1** — **author line?** (first clause) names: 4 (Jinduk, Sacred Bone, Bidam) plus an age in parentheses. Why it glazes: the reader has known her as Seungman for six entries and is never told the two names are the same woman.
  - Before: "Queen Jinduk (47) is crowned before the blood on the yard dries — Sacred Bone’s last polite miracle, stamped and filed while the censers are still warm…"
  - After (EN): "Seungman is crowned Queen Jinduk before the blood on the yard dries. The bloodline’s last polite miracle, stamped and filed while the censers are still warm. The succession Bidam died objecting to passes at last. Unanimously."
  - After (KO): "마당의 피가 마르기도 전에 승만이 진덕여왕으로 즉위한다. 그 핏줄의 마지막 점잖은 기적, 향로가 식기도 전에 도장 찍혀 철해진다. 비담이 반대하다 죽은 계승이 마침내 통과된다. 만장일치로."

### Huangdi (皇帝) (#46)
- **b1 / b27** — **author line?** "Prince Chunchu (45) approaches the Second Emperor and offers an alliance, vowing revenge against Baekje." appears twice, word for word. Keep b1 and cut b27 (the go-board room already plays the alliance).
- **b2** — names: 4 (Chang’an, Zhongshu, Menxia, Shangshu). Why it glazes: three Chinese department names that no reader will hold onto.
  - Before: "In Chang’an he watches the machine that does not wait for uncles: Zhongshu drafts, Menxia examines, Shangshu executes through six boards. One seal. One speed."
  - After (EN): "In Chang’an he watches a machine that doesn’t wait for uncles. One office drafts. One checks. One carries it out through six boards. One seal. One speed."
  - After (KO): "장안에서 그는 삼촌들을 기다리지 않는 기계를 본다. 한 관청이 기안한다. 한 관청이 살핀다. 한 관청이 여섯 부서로 집행한다. 어보 하나. 속도 하나."
- **b4** — the banner joke stays. Only the approach sentence is clogged (Mingde Gate, Zhuque Avenue). Change only the first sentence and keep every banner line word for word.
  - Before: "The embassy comes in by the Mingde Gate at the hour the street drums stop, and Zhuque Avenue opens ahead of it, a hundred and fifty paces wide and perfectly empty…"
  - After (EN): "The embassy comes in at the hour the street drums stop. The great avenue opens ahead of it, a hundred and fifty paces wide and perfectly empty."
  - After (KO): "사절단은 거리의 북이 멎는 시각에 들어선다. 눈앞에 대로가 열린다. 폭이 백오십 보, 완벽하게 텅 비어 있다."
- **b49** — names: 6 (Ministry of War, Chunchu, Historiography Office, Chu Suiliang). Why it glazes: two ministries and a name in two sentences, plus an appositive résumé.
  - Before: "Since the Ministry of War cannot find him a general, Chunchu tries the Historiography Office. Chu Suiliang receives him among the shelves: the man who once refused to let the emperor read his own diary…"
  - After (EN): "The Ministry of War can’t find him a general, so Chunchu tries the historians. Chu Suiliang receives him among the shelves. He once refused to let the emperor read his own diary. Now he’s high enough to choose what he says, and careful enough to say very little."
  - After (KO): "병부가 장수를 찾아 주지 못하자 춘추는 사관들을 찾아간다. 저수량이 서가 사이에서 그를 맞는다. 한때 황제가 제 일기를 읽지 못하게 막은 사람이다. 이제는 무슨 말을 할지 고를 만큼 높고, 거의 아무 말도 하지 않을 만큼 조심스럽다."
- **b152** — names: 1 (Daming). Why it glazes: it is an image prompt pasted into the narration ("not a lamp in the frame", "the reverse of a magenta plane"). The style rule forbids art-direction notes in `p`.
  - Before: "The Daming flying corridor is night — vermilion columns, white plaster, a red line at the brick floor. Faint court-light from the next hall, not a lamp in the frame. She is porcelain-pale…"
  - After (EN): "Night in a long palace corridor. Red columns, white plaster, a little light leaking from the next hall. Somewhere a banquet is still going. Out here it’s quiet enough to hear footsteps behind you."
  - After (KO): "밤, 궁궐의 긴 회랑. 붉은 기둥, 흰 회벽, 옆 전각에서 새어 나오는 희미한 빛. 어딘가에선 아직 연회가 이어진다. 여기는 뒤따라오는 발소리가 들릴 만큼 조용하다."
- **b181** — names: 4 (Tang, Goguryeo, 순라선, Chunchu, Yeon) plus a gloss. Why it glazes: there is a Hangul gloss in the English line.
  - Before: "The embassy is a day and a night out of the Tang coast when a second hull takes their weather. Not a war-fleet. A Goguryeo patrol ship, 순라선, the kind that tastes a road and reports who used it…"
  - After (EN): "A day and a night out to sea, a second hull takes their wind. Not a war fleet. A Goguryeo patrol boat, the kind that sniffs a sea-road and reports who used it. They’ve been sniffing this one since Chunchu walked out of Yeon’s prison."
  - After (KO): "바다로 나선 지 하루 낮 하룻밤, 또 다른 배 한 척이 그들의 바람을 가로챈다. 함대가 아니다. 고구려의 순라선, 바닷길 냄새를 맡고 누가 지나갔는지 보고하는 배다. 그 배들은 춘추가 연의 감옥을 걸어 나온 그해부터 이 길을 맡아 왔다."
- **b188** — told twice: it restates the `quote` at b187 (the queen grieves, the posthumous rank, the descendants paid), and "Daeachan" is an office string. Keep only the first sentence.
  - Before: "He reaches the home shore in a boat Chang’an would not have counted. Queen Jinduk hears and grieves. She posthumously names Gunhae a Daeachan, and the treasury pays his descendants."
  - After (EN): "He reaches the home shore in a boat Chang’an wouldn’t have bothered to count."
  - After (KO): "그는 장안이라면 셀 생각도 안 했을 작은 배로 고향 바닷가에 닿는다."

### Royal Secretariat (#47)
- **b22** — names: 6 (Chang’an, Surabol, Silla, Bupmin, Jinduk, Ode to Great Peace, Third Emperor). Why it glazes: too many names, and "the Third Emperor" gives away the Second Emperor's death one entry before *Jiabeng*.
  - Before: "The chest of court robes that came home from Chang’an is opened in the first month of the next year. By spring every official in Surabol above a certain rank has been measured for one…"
  - After (EN): "The chest of court robes from the west is opened at the new year. By spring every senior official has been measured for one. A year later the kingdom stops counting its own years and starts counting the emperor’s. Bupmin sails west with the queen’s ode woven into a length of silk. The emperor in Chang’an admires it extravagantly."
  - After (KO): "서쪽에서 온 관복 상자가 새해 첫 달에 열린다. 봄이 되자 높은 관리들은 모두 치수를 잰다. 이듬해 나라는 제 연호를 버리고 황제의 연호를 센다. 법민이 여왕의 송가를 짜 넣은 비단 한 필을 들고 서쪽으로 간다. 장안의 황제는 그것을 요란하게 칭찬한다."
- **b4** — names: 0. Why it glazes: a decoder paragraph ("Anyone who thinks… has misread the man; what he brings home is a grammar") with a semicolon, explaining the scene before it plays.
  - Before: "Anyone who thinks he is copying a banquet toast has misread the man; what he brings home is a grammar. One seal. One speed. Fewer uncles…"
  - After (EN): "What he brought home from the west is a grammar. One seal. One speed. Fewer uncles. When the old council finally falls, nobody will proclaim it. It will just be a table that has never held a feast."
  - After (KO): "그가 서쪽에서 가져온 건 문법이다. 어보 하나. 속도 하나. 줄어든 삼촌들. 옛 회의가 마침내 무너질 때, 아무도 그것을 선포하지 않을 것이다. 잔치를 치러 본 적 없는 탁자 하나가 있을 뿐이다."
- **b28** — spoiler, not names. "Twelve years later his successors try it at the White River with four hundred ships, and the sea fills them instead" gives away the White River outcome in passing.
  - Before: "Emperor Kōtoku does not fill the sea. Twelve years later his successors try it at the White River with four hundred ships, and the sea fills them instead."
  - After (EN): "Emperor Kōtoku does not fill the sea. His successors will remember the idea."
  - After (KO): "고토쿠 천황은 바다를 메우지 않는다. 그의 후계자들이 그 생각을 기억해 둘 것이다."

### Jiabeng (駕崩) (#48)
- **b15 / b16** — **author lines?** Flag only. "King Euija (49)" and "Gyebek (29)" put ages in parentheses, which is file-card style. If touched, drop the parentheses: "Euija grows more watchful of the great clans." / "Gyebek already knows what the silence means."

### King Muyeol (#49)
- **b0** — names: 3 in one sentence (Jinduk, Sunduk, Chunchu ×2). Why it glazes: an appositive family chart, then a semicolon.
  - Before: "For seven years the crown has sat on Queen Jinduk — Sunduk’s cousin, Chunchu’s aunt in the house’s counting — while the work sat on Chunchu’s table. No one has ever called her foolish; she is simply outnumbered by seals."

## The 5 worst paragraphs in this range

1. **Four Dragons b28.** Sixteen flagged tokens: three foreign personal names, a tribe and a khan title, and none of them comes back. The dragon colours alone carry the beat.
2. **Yodong b18.** Eleven names: a roll-call of forts and lords the reader never sees. The beat ("the line falls; two forts stand") is buried.
3. **승 (承) b10.** An office, an age, a title, a gloss and two fortress names before the first verb, in the opening of a countdown that needs speed.
4. **Seohyun b151.** An office string, a province, a march and a variant name in what should be a quiet farewell to Seohyeon.
5. **Huangdi b152.** The worst kind of clog: an image prompt ("not a lamp in the frame", "the reverse of a magenta plane") printed as narration.

Also worth fixing even though they are not name-clogged:
- **Ansi b24** says "Li Shimin" eleven entries before *Huangdi*, where saying that name aloud is the climax.
- **Royal Secretariat b22 and b28** give away, in passing, the Second Emperor's death and the White River outcome.
- **The Eastern Star b15** explains Jumong's cave before his myth episode.
- **Huangdi b27** repeats b1 word for word.

## Names that should be wiki-only (never on the page)

- **Tang court and army:** Ashina She’er, Qibi Heli, Zhangsun Wuji (keep their dragon colours), Prince of Jiangxia, Yan Lide, Fu Fuai (Ansi b21: say "the officer who left the mound"), Zhang Shigui, the Xueyantuo, Laizhou, the Zhongshu / Menxia / Shangshu departments, Mingde Gate, Zhuque Avenue, Ganye Temple, Liu Yingchun.
- **Goguryeo forts and garrisons:** Hyeondo, Gaemo, Gasi (it may stay in Taizong's line), Baegam, Son Daeeum, Ogol, Bisa, Geonan. Keep Sinseong as "the New Fortress".
- **Silla councils and clans:** Supum, Euljé, Imjong (Murim and Suljong may speak, but shouldn't be listed in narration), Surabol Son / Musan / Gurema in narration (the dialogue may keep them).
- **Yushin's family trivia:** Heumsun, A-hae, A-ji, Bohui, Soyeon, Jincheon (the later name of Manno), Taeryeong (it can stay inside the `quote`), Geonbok era years.
- **Myth asides:** Ubal (the shallows), Ijinasi (as long as only Suro matters), Okmun-gok and Doksan Fortress as separate labels (one name is enough: Jade Gate).
- **Office titles in English narration:** Sangdaedeung, Daeachan, sopan, Governor-General, Left Militant Guard, Master of Works. Use the plain English role or drop it.
